html:
SMTO-CMP-0015 — The AI tried to finish using a step that can't prove it

GUID: b18d5776-3462-4bd1-b1db-cb6afcaef5bc
Slug: completion-ineligible-direct-result
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model tried to end the task on a step that didn't run successfully or isn't a normal tool result, so SMTO didn't accept that as the finish. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's last step to see whether it ran successfully, failed or didn't run. Only a step that ran successfully can end the task this way.
  2. If it failed, check the real system to see whether anything changed anyway. A failed step can still change something, and SMTO shouldn't do it twice.
  3. Select Resume, or describe what's done and what's left in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task, then select Continue. SMTO then finishes through its normal check using results it already has.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure what already happened. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so changes could happen twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its final reply appears under it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task while it's unclear whether the last step changed anything.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Direct completion had no registered capability or current operation result, the result's operation_id did not match, or the result was not an executed success or completed outcome (reason ineligible_direct_result).

What this means

  • Direct completion lacks a registered capability/current operation result, mismatches operation_id, or has no executed successful/completed result. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Direct completion lacks a registered capability/current operation result, mismatches operation_id, or has no executed successful/completed result.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact operation identity, registered capability and execution status before choosing the ordinary finish flow.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the pending call's capability mapping, operation_id and the result's executed and status fields (attempt_direct_completion validate in src/agent_runtime/native/direct_completion.py). Resume so the model completes through finish_task with eligible original receipts; do not re-execute the operation to obtain a fresh direct-completion result.
  • Use the supported finish_task completion flow with appropriate evidence for this result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported finish_task validation uses eligible original evidence for the actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
